error_message: rank.test: 23×17 expected 'difference-of-squares' top, got 'place-value-split' (three-way tie at 4.75)
root_cause: Cost model charged 400−9 two borrow penalties, but subtracting a single digit from a round number is trivial mentally; also round-down-compensate produced a tree identical to place-value-split, inflating the tie.
fix: Skip borrow penalty when subtrahend ≤ 10 in cost.ts; dedupe identical step trees (by joined step exprs) in rank.ts after sorting.

error_message: TS2345 in leftToRight.ts: Type '"square"' is not assignable to type 'StepOp' (passing Problem.op where StepOp expected)
root_cause: Problem['op'] ('add'|'sub'|'mul'|'div'|'square'|'pct') is wider than StepOp; applies() narrows to add/sub at runtime but TS can't see it inside expand().
fix: Compute `adding = p.op === 'add'` once and pass the literal 'add'/'sub' to step().

error_message: rank.test: 77×5 expected 'place-value-split' top, got 'round-down-compensate' (1.75 vs 2.50) after research-calibrated weight update
root_cause: New graded table-fact tiers put 7×5 in the large tier (−1.0) while the anchor discount rose to −0.75 AND anchor results (375) double-dipped the %25 round-number bonus — recreating the exact regression in Do-Not-Repeat.
fix: Two evidence-grounded adjustments: (1) easy fact tier = tie || min factor ≤ 3 || a five operand (the documented fives effect); (2) round-number bonus narrowed to multiples of 10 — odd multiples of 25 are priced by the anchor discount, not the round bonus.

error_message: quarter-anchor wrongly topped 16×25 (0.45) after audit-v2 recalibration; rank.test '16×25: factor-and-regroup is top' failed
root_cause: anchor facts were converted from a discount off the procedural base to a flat retrieval net of 0.75, which priced two-digit anchor products (16×25) as cheap as single-digit facts
fix: restored anchor semantics as a discount: factNet returns base − anchorFactDiscount (0.75) for kind 'anchor', so the net scales with the procedural base (16×25 → 3.5−0.75)
